deletedGuardsInvisibleToSAST.briefCorrection: The task brief states that run-02's seed SA-004 keyed on the now-deleted strict equality. That is not what run-02's artifact says: run-02's SA-004 is `slither:low-level-calls` at src/Antimatter.sol:292 (the decimals() staticcall in toStableAmount), and it is STILL LIVE at 3a96fb7 (now line 295, normalised below as SA-004). The strict-equality item is run-01's SA-004, which run-02 filed under `resolvedSinceRun01`, not under `findings`. Both are reported here so neither is lost.
consequenceForTriage: The minter's own quote is no longer consulted at all, so a short mint relative to the quote can no longer be detected by the contract - only a shortfall relative to the CALLER's floor.

minPhUSDOut is compared against `amount + mintedForStable`, i.e. the antimatter half is counted toward the floor. The antimatter half is always exactly `amount` and is never at risk, so a caller passing minPhUSDOut <= amount gets a check that can never bind. The NatSpec states passing zero waives protection; it does not state that any value at or below `amount` waives it equally.

The test suite records the behavioural inversion directly: `test_overPhUSDMintReverts` was DELETED and `test_overPhUSDMintNowSucceeds` added, alongside `test_shortPhUSDMintClearingFloorSucceeds`. A short mint that still clears the floor is now an accepted outcome by design. Whether that is faithful to story-003 is a Law-2 question for story-faithfulness, not a SAST question.
Slither's naming-convention detector is the only tool that registered any of this, and only as noise on the test function names (see rawRecordDelta).

findings.description: Antimatter.toStableAmount(address,uint256) (src/Antimatter.sol#283-304) performs a multiplication on the result of a division: stableAmount = amount / scale (#301); stableAmount * scale != amount (#302).
findings.note: This is the deliberate exact-representability round-trip check (reverts AmountNotRepresentable if the division lost precision), not a precision bug. Carried at potential-medium for dedup continuity only; run-02 reached the same reading.

findings.rawCheck: M-1 Contracts are vulnerable to fee-on-transfer accounting-related issues
findings.description: IERC20(stable).safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), stableAmount) at line 246 assumes the full stableAmount arrives. A fee-on-transfer stablecoin delivers less; the subsequent forceApprove(minter, stableAmount) and minter.mint(stable, stableAmount) then operate on a quantity the contract does not hold.
findings.note: ESCALATED FOR TIER 2 - detector unchanged but its CONTEXT changed materially inside this delta. At c91bc1a the shortfall was backstopped indirectly: `mintedForStable != expectedForStable` compared the realised phUSD against the minter's own quote for stableAmount, so a fee-on-transfer discrepancy surfaced as a phUSD mismatch and reverted the whole call. story-003 DELETED that check. The remaining backstops are the measured-balance check `IERC20(stable).balanceOf(address(this)) != stableBefore` at 254 (which catches residue, not a fee) and the caller's own minPhUSDOut floor at 260. Note also that C4 treats fee-on-transfer tokens as a known-invalid class unless explicitly in scope; the finding is retained because the DELETED GUARD, not the token class, is the new fact. Dedup/severity to decide.

findings.description: Raw low-level call: (ok, data) = stable.staticcall(abi.encodeCall(IERC20Metadata.decimals, ())) at line 295, used to cross-check the minter's registered decimals against the token's own.
findings.note: STILL LIVE - this is run-02's SA-004, introduced by story-002, and story-003 did not touch it. It is NOT the strict-equality item (that is run-01's SA-004; see deletedGuardsInvisibleToSAST.briefCorrection). Not an unchecked-return defect: the return IS checked at 296 (`if (!ok || data.length != 32) revert DecimalsUnavailable(stable);`) then decoded and compared at 297-298. The open Tier-2 question is unchanged: toStableAmount hard-requires every registered stablecoin to answer decimals() with exactly 32 bytes, so a token without decimals() - or one behind a reverting proxy - makes annihilate() permanently unavailable for that stablecoin.

findings.rawCheck: L-3 Some tokens may revert when zero value transfers are made
findings.inDeltaWindowNote: Instance at 264 (safeTransfer of mintedForStable to recipient) is inside the story-003 window; instances at 246 and 311 are outside.
findings.description: Three unguarded transfer sites that some tokens revert on for a zero value: safeTransferFrom at 246, safeTransfer of mintedForStable at 264, token.safeTransfer at 311.
findings.note: Line 264 is newly interesting: with the quote-equality check deleted, mintedForStable is no longer constrained to a non-zero quote. A minter that mints zero phUSD for the stablecoin half now reaches line 264 with mintedForStable == 0, whereas at c91bc1a `expectedForStable == 0` reverted PhUSDNotReceived before any transfer. Tier 2 should decide whether a zero-mint annihilation is intended (the NatSpec at 222-225 says it is: 'at a zero exchange rate it means giving up the stablecoin half for nothing but the antimatter half'). Weird-ERC20 revert-on-zero is a C4 known-invalid class; the zero-mint REACHABILITY is the part that is not.
